newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols deteriorate as dollar stalls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols deteriorate as dollar stalls.

text.p: Implied volatility rates edged lower in dollar/yen and dropped more dramatically in dollar/mark as the U.S. currency backed off from key upside targets.

One-month dollar/mark was 8.65/8.85 percent at midday, down from 9.00/9.10 percent Tuesday, and one-year was 9.20/9.35 percent, down from 9.50/9.60 percent, as the spot retreated from the 1.7300 area. The dollar on Tuesday climbed to a new three-year high against the mark at 1.7364.

Growing sentiment that this month's Group of Seven meeting holds the key to the spot market's long-term trend led options traders to conclude that a period of range-bound activity was in store for the dollar.
"Everyone is waiting to see what will come out of the G-7 meeting," said a U.S. trader for a Japanese bank.

Sales of dollar/yen strangles have increased accordingly, with one large Japanese corporation noted selling 124.50 yen calls and 127.50 yen puts expiring April 25, one day before the G-7 is set to meet in Washington, traders said.

A "reverse knockout" option that vanishes if dollar/yen reaches 127.30 also caught the market's attention. The buyer of the option, said to be a Japanese insurance company, can be expected to step in and sell dollar/yen to defend the position if spot approaches 127.00, options traders said.

The trade's profitability increases as the dollar nears the 127.30 yen trigger, but becomes worthless if the level is hit. The seller of the option can be expected to try to push dollar/yen through the trigger.
"If spot goes up as high as 127.00, we'll see a fierce battle around there between the buyer and the seller of the option," the Japanese bank trader said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen Wednesday slipped to 9.10/9.30 percent from 9.20/9.35 the previous session, and one-year to 10.40/10.35 from 10.45/10.55.
With dollar bullishness appearing to subside, some traders have abandoned yen put positions, market participants said.
Dollar/yen one-month 25-delta risk reversals flip-flopped to flat/0.10 skewed to yen calls from 0.20/0.35 skewed to yen puts, though long-term reversals still favor the yen put side.
Short-term dollar/mark risk reversals continue to favor mark puts but had narrowed to flat/0.20 from 0.20/0.45.
Market participants downplayed the chance of Thursday's U.S. trade data having much impact on the dollar.
"It would take a highly unexpected number to make a difference," the bank trader said.
Another options trader for a Japanese bank identified 124.50 to 128.50 as dollar/yen's likely range from here and said volatility should stay subdued as long as the spot held to those parameters.
